title: Explicit quotient vertex of extension of scalars
statement: Let A,B,C be commutative rings in one universe, C an A-algebra, pi:A\to B a surjective ring homomorphism, and I=ker(pi). Put Q=C/IC, where IC=I.map(A\to C). Define H:CommAlgCat(A)\to CommAlgCat(B) by the equivalence with rings under A, pushout along pi, and the inverse equivalence for B. There exists a B-algebra structure on Q and an isomorphism H(C)\cong Q in CommAlgCat(B).

proof.text: The map A to C/IC kills I. Descend it uniquely along the surjection pi using RingHom.liftOfSurjective; its kernel condition follows from Ideal.le_comap_map.
Define the B-algebra action by this descended ring map. The quotient map C to C/IC and the descended map B to C/IC agree on A.
For any compatible maps C to T and B to T, the first map kills IC by Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap and the kernel equation. Ideal.Quotient.lift supplies the unique map from C/IC to T.

Check the two factorization equations; the B equation can be checked after pi by surjectivity. Uniqueness follows from surjectivity of C to C/IC. PushoutCocone.isColimitAux verifies the universal property.
Use uniqueness of pushouts to obtain an isomorphism under B, then map it through the inverse equivalence to CommAlgCat(B).

mathlib_searches.query: pushout of a surjective commutative ring map is a quotient by the extended kernel ideal

mathlib_searches.results: CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct; no categorical quotient-action interface matching this statement
Types pushout as quotient; no ring quotient interface. Existing lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change is a tensor equivalence, not the pushout-under-B interface used here.

theorem quotientBaseChange_obj_iso
    (A B C : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    (π : A →+* B) (hπ : Function.Surjective π)
    (I : Ideal A) (hker : RingHom.ker π = I) :
    ∃ (_ : Algebra B (C ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A C))),
      Nonempty ((quotientBaseChange π).obj (CommAlgCat.of A C) ≅
        CommAlgCat.of B (C ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A C)))
